faqs.a: Surround text with markers: *bold*, _italic_, ~strikethrough~, `code`, ```code block```, and start a line with > for a quote. WhatsApp renders these automatically; this tool shows you the result in advance.
faqs.q: How does WhatsApp text formatting work?

faqs.a: Paste any text that uses WhatsApp markers. The preview renders them as formatted HTML; the Strip markup mode removes every marker and leaves plain text.
faqs.q: What does this tool do with my chat text?

faqs.a: This tool only reads the text you paste — it cannot see your WhatsApp account, contacts or chats. Never paste anything you would not want to share.
faqs.q: Can it read my WhatsApp chats directly?

faqs.a: Use the Strip markup mode, which removes every formatting marker and quote symbol, leaving clean plain text ready for reports or archives.
faqs.q: How do I remove all formatting from copied chat text?

faqs.q: Can I use the formatted output on my website?

faqs.a: The preview is a close approximation using standard HTML tags. WhatsApp's own app may space things slightly differently, but bold, italic, strikethrough, code and quotes all match.
faqs.q: Does the preview match WhatsApp exactly?

faqs.a: No. The conversion runs entirely in your browser with JavaScript. Nothing is sent anywhere.

limitations: The parser is regex-based, so edge cases differ from WhatsApp: underscores inside words (like snake_case) may be read as italic markers.
Nested formatting (bold inside italic) renders approximately, not exactly like WhatsApp.
The preview approximates WhatsApp's styling; exact fonts and spacing belong to the WhatsApp app.
This tool cannot access your WhatsApp account or import chats — you must paste the text yourself.

whatsapp-text-formatter.workedExample: Input: *Hello* _world_ ~oops~ `code` Step 1: escape HTML (no change here) Step 2: no ```blocks``` to extract Step 3: `code` -> code Step 4: *Hello* -> Hello Step 5: _world_ -> world Step 6: ~oops~ -> oops Preview renders: Hello (bold) world (italic) oops (struck through) code (monospace). Strip markup mode deletes every * _ ~ ` and returns: "Hello world oops code".
mistakes: Expecting it to read your chats directly — it cannot access WhatsApp; you paste the text yourself, nothing is uploaded.
Copying the HTML preview into WhatsApp — WhatsApp needs the *markup*, not rendered HTML; use the markup copy.
Stripping markup and expecting emphasis to survive — plain text has no bold or italic, so meaning carried by formatting is lost.
Assuming formatting works everywhere — strikethrough and monospace render in WhatsApp but vanish in SMS and email.
Pasting formatted text into a plain-text field — bios and usernames often strip the asterisks and show them literally.
